Share on X (Opens in new window) X Share on Facebook (Opens in new window) Facebook Add Us On Google One major creator has returned to the pages of Shueisha's Weekly Shonen Jump magazine only a year after their previous series came to an end, and has kicked things off with a special crossover to help celebrate. Shonen Jump has entered its final transitional period for the year as a number of titles have kicked off their own serializations as fans say goodbye to some of the longer running hits . But with this go around, some of these new titles are from experienced creators.

Hitsuji Gondaira wrapped up Mission: Yozakura Family 's run with Shonen Jump last year , and has already made his return to the magazine with the start of a new series. Making its debut over the weekend, Hizuki of the Ginza Patrol offers a much different kind of story than seen with the chaotic spy adventures of Gondaira's previous work. As a special way to celebrate the new debut, Gondaira has released a special crossover with Hizuki and Taiyo joining the Ginza Patrol. Check it out below.

Hizuki of the Ginza Patrol made its full debut with Shonen Jump this past weekend , and the first chapter of the new series offers an entirely different kind of story than fans had seen with Mission: Yozakura Family. While that series offered an extended cast as Taiyo joined a huge family of spies, this new series doesn't go that route. Instead fans are introduced to Osamu Hizuki, a samurai who's come out of the war with the intent of living a life enjoying the new era and its technologies.

Hizuki of the Ginza Patrol already seems a lot more focused when it comes to its core cast as there's really only Hizuki and his new partner Rin. She's the first girl to join the patrol, and is only doing so to eventually solve the murder of her mother. Hizuki was one of the most deadly samurai in the war, but hopes to leave that life behind eventually and enjoy his new life. We'll see how this all develops as the series hopefully gets the chance to have as long of a run as Mission: Yozakura Family was able to before it ended .

Shonen Jump is an incredibly fickle magazine as this year alone has already seen 14 different titles come to their ends. Only six of those releases were titles that were able to come to their natural conclusions , and all of the others had been cancelled shortly into their respective runs. It's hard to tell at this point if Gondaira's newest work has any real chance of success, but it's likely to avoid cancellation at least for a while since it's a returning creator already familiar with how Shonen Jump operates.

That's not always the best thing for Shonen Jump , however, as even some returning creators have had their new works cancelled after short runs. It doesn't matter how successful their prior work is either as with notable cases like Masashi Kishimoto's Samurai 8 getting cancelled after a few months despite how big of a runaway hit Naruto was before. It's all a toss up.

How are you feeling about Hizuki of the Ginza Patrol so far? Do you think it has a chance at success with Shonen Jump ? Let us know all of your thoughts about it in the comments.

articles.title: "Alarming" Diversity Backtrack Happening In Film and TV Industry In Canada, Report Finds
articles.summary: Despite homegrown hits like 'Heated Rivalry' and 'North of North,' the Writers Guild of Canada warns “key barriers” to future work stand in the way of new diverse members joining its ranks.
articles.content:
As the Canadian film and TV industry remains committed to diversity, equity and inclusion, resisting pressures to backtrack in a post-Trump DEI rollback era, aspiring diverse screenwriters now find themselves struggling to advance in a shrinking business.

So says the Writers Guild of Canada in its latest Equity, Diversity and Inclusion report released on Tuesday.

While the guild pointed to more diverse screenwriters joining its Canadian ranks, WGC executive director Victoria Shen revealed in the report “alarming numbers that affect not only diverse writers, but all Canadian screenwriters. This is the second year in a row in which we saw a decline in the number of episodes across every production format covered by the report. While we have seen decreases in Canadian production in the past, these numbers demonstrate an industry in decline.”

The EDI report accounted for diverse writers in the WGC ranks by measuring the number of black, indigenous, LGBTQ2S, people of color and people with disabilities. And the percentage of diverse members in the WGC membership rose to 51 percent in 2025, up from 42 percent in 2024 and 33 percent in 2019.

Despite that membership growth, the 2026 EDI report pointed to the number of writers earning over CAN$200,000 (US$140,000) being highest among white, cisgender, heterosexual and non-disabled writer, while half of black writers and those with disabilities earned less than CAN$20,000 (US$14,000) in 2025, the last year measured.

Amid mounting industry disruption, domestic broadcasters continue to lose market share to foreign streamers, who in turn face no local content spending obligations to offset lower investment in the Canadian ecosystem. And that’s impacting diverse Canadian writers who rely on local content investment to get in the door and build careers.

“One of the key barriers to their advancement is the depressed state of the industry and the lack of opportunities for anyone, which is compounded and made more acute by their diverse identities,” Shen insisted. The Canadian TV industry has faced a continuing contraction as audiences and advertising dollars shift to U.S. streamers and other digital platforms.

And that has implications for Canadian sovereignty versus the country’s southern neighbor amid U.S. President Donald Trump’s ongoing tariff war and taunts about Canada becoming the 51st state.

“Investment in Canadian culture is more important now than ever. The loss of jobs for Canadian screenwriters is the bellwether that spells the loss of our screens to foreign creators. But this time of profound change is also an opportunity to reimagine what is possible. We can do more than defend Canadian culture: we should realize its economic potential, bolster its cultural reach and export it. Investing in Canadian screenwriting and domestic production is how we start to reverse the decline and reform the industry,” Shen argued.

The latest EDI report from the WGC surveyed 141 series live-action and animation series produced in 2024 and 2025, in addition to the 448 series covered from 2019 to 2023.

The guild found a steep decline in production numbers from 2018 to 2025, including 29 percent fewer one hour drama episodes at the end of that period, and 28 percent half-hour adult series episodes.

The WGC also pointed to even steeper cuts in the number of kids live action and animation episodes.

articles.title: Fans of Nathan Fillion's Wrongly Canceled Sci-Fi Western Series Can Grab His Screen-Matched Pistol for $15,000
articles.summary: Courtesy of 20th Century Studios When it comes to TV shows that were canceled before their time, there are a handful that still sting no matter how much time passes. Among them is a sci-fi series that debuted in 2002 to almost perfect reviews from audiences but didn't even make it to the end of its first season before being […]
articles.content:
Share on X (Opens in new window) X Share on Facebook (Opens in new window) Facebook Add Us On Google When it comes to TV shows that were canceled before their time, there are a handful that still sting no matter how much time passes. Among them is a sci-fi series that debuted in 2002 to almost perfect reviews from audiences but didn't even make it to the end of its first season before being canceled, much to the annoyance of those who had very quickly come to love it. Starring Nathan Fillion, Firefly is one of the biggest missed chances in TV history, and even though there has been talk of a possible revival , a live-action return has not happened so far. Yet the love for the series among fans has never waned, and now thanks to Prop Store fans have the chance to own the Liberty Hammer pistol used by Fillion in his role as Captain Malcolm Reynolds, but it won't come cheap.

The sidearm that is up for auction is not just a regular prop gun either. This one has been screen-matched to Firefly sequel movie Serenity , after being used in the series first and later modified with a removable magazine. It is also one of only two weapons made for the show that could actually be fired. The gun was adapted from a real Taurus Model 85 revolver, with brass-colored frame, a spring-loaded slider, and brown wooden grips. Although the piece was real at the time of filming, the gun has since been fully deactivated and comes with a certificate of proof. Of course, this means that the price tag will reflect the scarcity of the item, and after already hitting its starting bid of $15,000 the estimate suggests that price will rise to up to $60,000. If the right interested parties are in attendance as the auction closes on December 4, then the final price could end even higher.

There are not many TV shows that are canceled after one season then go on to be among some of the most-loved and remembered. Firefly only managed to air 11 episodes before being pulled from schedules by Fox, with three additional episodes never airing. However, when the series was released on DVD, the show gained a cult following that refused to let it die. This momentum was enough for the characters from the series to get a second chance with a big screen adventure in Serenity . The movie released in 2005 to rave reviews just like Firefly , even if its box office did not match the praise. The film ended up making $40 million, but considering its $39 million budget it did not spark any studio interest in reviving the series or developing a sequel no matter how much the fandom wanted it.

Many members of the Firefly cast have gone on to bigger things, including Morena Baccarin, Alan Tudyk , and, of course, Fillion, who most recently became the DCU's new Green Lantern in 2025's Superman . However, even 23 years after their last outing, the cast of Firefly have not given up on coming back together for a revival and it is now happening in an animated series . Yet the idea of the show being brought back to life in a live-action format has also not gone away. While there are certainly no guarantees of that coming to fruition, there could not be a better time for Firefly to make a return with streamers constantly looking for their next hit. Could it be possible for a new series of Firefly to actually make it to screens and be the success that was denied of its first run? Stranger things have happened.

Would you love to see Firefly return? Let us know in the comments.

articles.content:
Black Friday is one of the best times of year to reassess your streaming subscriptions. Following another year of price hikes across Hollywood’s biggest streaming services, nearly every major platform is offering steep discounts on monthly and annual subscriptions ahead of the holiday weekend.

Among this year’s standout deals are HBO Max ‘s yearlong subscription for just $5.49 a month, Apple TV’s six-month subscription for $6.99 a month and two-months of Paramount+ for $2.99 a month — including its normally pricier, ad-free Premium plan . Meanwhile, Peacock is back with a Black Friday promo after sitting out last year’s sales event, and Disney+ and Hulu have once again slashed the price of their streaming bundle. Related Stories Amazon Debuts $30 Streaming Bundle That Includes Starz, BritBox, AMC+, MGM+ and PBS Masterpiece In One Place Celebrity Streaming and Commerce Platform TalkShopLive Expands to TikTok Ahead of Black Friday

Most of this year’s streaming deals run through Cyber Monday, Nov. 30, and are available to new and eligible returning subscribers.

Below, check out the best Black Friday streaming deals to take advantage of this year.

$6.99/Month for Six Months (53% Off)

Through Nov. 30, eligible subscribers can sign up for six months of Apple TV for $6.99 a month, down from its regular monthly price of $14.99. The promotion, available across 40 markets worldwide, saves U.S. subscribers $48 over the course of six months.

Original programming includes Emmy-winning series such as “Severance,” “The Studio” and “Ted Lasso,” in addition to acclaimed dramas such as “Slow Horses,” “Pluribus” and “Shrinking.” Among its upcoming releases is “Neuromancer,” Apple’s highly anticipated adaptation of William Gibson’s seminal science-fiction novel.

$2.99/Month for Two Months (Up to 79% Off)

Paramount+ has brought back one of its steepest subscription discounts of the year, offering both its ad-supported Essential plan and its largely ad-free Premium plan for $2.99 a month for the first two months.

In addition to Showtime programming such as “Yellowjackets,” the streamer is home to Taylor Sheridan’s sprawling television empire, including “Landman,” “Tulsa King” and “Dutton Ranch,” alongside franchises such as “South Park,” “Star Trek” and “Mission: Impossible.” It’s also one of the better streaming options for sports fans, with coverage of the NFL on CBS, UEFA Champions League and UFC events.

Starting at $2.99/Month (Up to 66% Off)

After forgoing a Black Friday deal last year, Peacock is offering discounts across two of its subscription tiers this year. Its Select plan, which includes programming from NBC, Bravo and Telemundo, is available for $2.99 a month for three months or $29.99 for an entire year.

Those looking for access to Peacock’s full programming library can sign up for its Premium plan for $8.99 a month for three months or $89.99 for a year, down from its usual annual price of $129.99.

The latter is the better option for those looking to stream live sports, movies and Peacock originals such as “The Traitors,” “The Paper” and “All Her Fault.” Premium subscribers can also tune into the Macy’s Thanksgiving Day Parade, NFL games, NBA matchups and Premier League soccer.

Starting at $4.99/Month for 12 Months

Disney+ and Hulu are once again teaming up for one of the best yearlong streaming deals of Black Friday. Through Nov. 30, the ad-supported Disney+ and Hulu bundle is down to $4.99 a month for 12 months. This year, the companies are also offering a discount on their Premium bundle, which brings the price of ad-free streaming across both platforms down to $14.99 a month for a year.

The bundle encompasses Disney’s extensive collection of Marvel, Pixar and “Star Wars” programming, alongside Hulu and FX hits such as “The Bear,” “Only Murders in the Building,” “Shōgun” and “The Secret Lives of Mormon Wives.”

Up to 79% Off Streaming Subscriptions

Amazon is slashing prices across dozens of Prime Video add-on subscriptions. Through Nov. 30, subscribers can sign up for AMC+, Starz, MGM+, BritBox and more for as little as $1.99 a month, in addition to taking advantage of the same discounted Apple TV, HBO Max and Paramount+ subscriptions available directly through the streamers.

Subscribers can get AMC+, MGM+ and Starz together for just $5.49 a month for two months, down from $21.99. Meanwhile, anime fans can score six months of Crunchyroll starting at $3.99 a month, while Hallmark+ is down to $2.25 a month just in time for the network’s annual slate of holiday movies.

Amazon is also discounting digital purchases of Christmas classics, including “The Polar Express,” “A Christmas Story” and “The Grinch,” starting at $7.99 apiece through Nov. 26.

$5.49/Month for 12 Months (50% Off)

HBO Max is slashing the price of its Basic With Ads plan by 50% for an entire year, bringing its monthly subscription down from $10.99 to $5.49. The deal, which runs through Nov. 30, amounts to $66 in annual savings.

The streamer’s highly anticipated “Harry Potter and the Philosopher’s Stone” series premieres on Christmas Day, followed by the third season of “The Pitt” in January. New seasons of “Heated Rivalry,” “The White Lotus,” “The Last of Us” and “A Knight of the Seven Kingdoms” are also slated for 2027.

In the meantime, subscribers can catch up on the fourth season of “The Gilded Age” and recent theatrical releases such as “Backrooms” and “The End of Oak Street,” alongside HBO staples such as “Succession,” “The Sopranos” and “Game of Thrones.”

articles.content:
Share on X (Opens in new window) X Share on Facebook (Opens in new window) Facebook Add Us On Google LEGO has announced a new collaboration with Marvel Rivals that will see one of the game's most popular characters recreated in brick form. Since launching back in 2024, Marvel Rivals has continued to be one of the most popular multiplayer games across consoles and PC. While the game features playable versions of Marvel icons like Spider-Man, Hulk, Captain America, and Iron Man, it has also introduced some much lesser-known Marvel characters that players have become more familiar with. Now, one of these breakout stars of Marvel Rivals has become so beloved in their own right that LEGO has opted to create a new toy based on their in-game look.

Revealed today on LEGO's official websit e, the toy manufacturer showed off a first glimpse of a new model for the character Jeff the Land Shark. Upon the arrival of Marvel Rivals , Jeff was one of the first playable characters on the game's roster. Although he was relatively unknown at the time, Jeff has since become arguably the face of Marvel Rivals , and remains one of its most beloved Marvel heroes nearly two years after its launch.

As for this LEGO version of Jeff the Land Shark, it's set to launch right at the start of 2027 on January 1st. The set, which is number #67023, includes 495 pieces in total and will come in at a price of $49.99. Generally speaking, this is a pretty solid price-per-piece value, which should lead to Jeff the Land Shark becoming one of the more popular and cost-effective LEGO sets to begin the new year.

You can get a look at this Jeff the Land Shark LEGO model for yourself right here:

Moving forward, there's a chance that LEGO could look to release more products that are tied to characters from Marvel Rivals . However, if this were to happen, LEGO would likely have to find a way to differentiate these sets from the countless other Marvel products it has released over the years. Characters like Spider-Man, Iron Man, and Hulk are no stranger to having been remade in LEGO fashion, which means that the brand would likely have to figure out what would set them apart if they were to get recreated in a Marvel Rivals -style. It's hard to know just now what this might look like, but it's still promising to think about as we look ahead to the future.

How do you feel about this new LEGO Jeff the Land Shark model? Are you planning to pick it up for yourself in January, or will you instead be holding off for other upcoming LEGO releases? Be sure to let me know your own thoughts down in the comments section.

articles.content:
Thank goodness for Aunt Gladys. If it weren't for last year's fright-wigged "Weapons" villainess — a bracing figure of pure, malicious evil amid cinema's recent run of goody-two-shoes witches, sparkling up the likes of "Wicked" and "Practical Magic 2" — you'd begin to worry that screen sorcery has altogether lost its edge. Not that there's anything wrong with humanizing witches per se , but surely we can all agree that the bad ones have more fun. The new Disney animated feature " Hexed " splits the difference. Its suburban teenage heroine Billie is about as wholesome a witch as witchery has ever seen, but at least she enjoys her powers, instead of moping about them: After the "Wicked" films spent nearly five hours telling us it's not easy being green, the chief takeaway of the bright, chipper "Hexed" is that witchin' is bitchin'. blogherads.adq.push(function () { blogherads .defineSlot( 'medrec', 'gpt-variety-article-mid-article-uid0' ) .setTargeting( 'pos', ["mid-article1","mid-articleX","mid","mid-article"] ) .setTargeting( 'viewable', 'yes' ) .setSubAdUnitPath("ros\/mid-article") .addSize([[300,250],[2,2],[300,251],[2,4],[4,2],[320,480],[620,366],[300,450]]) .setClsOptimization("minsize") ; }); Related Stories Amazon Debuts $30 Streaming Bundle That Includes Starz, BritBox, AMC+, MGM+ and PBS Masterpiece In One Place Celebrity Streaming and Commerce Platform TalkShopLive Expands to TikTok Ahead of Black Friday

There's not a whole lot more to it than that, however, even as Fawn Veerasunthorn and Jason Hand 's film attempts to squeeze a mother-daughter bonding tale in amidst all the magical hijinks. "Hexed" is ostensibly the first original animated film from the Disney stable since 2023's swiftly forgotten "Wish," but it certainly doesn't feel that way: Quilting together story elements from any number of previous, occult-tinged coming-of-age tales, it's about as familiar as, well, a witch's right-hand cat: Even its lurid violet-and-jade color palette looks secondhand so soon after "Wicked's" ubiquitous green-and-pink branding.

From its cookie-cutter characterization to its throwback design elements to a soundtrack embellished with familiar pop songs, the film is altogether too risk-averse to threaten classic status. That its narrative, about an ordinary American girl stumbling into an enchanted realm and discovering her hidden supernatural genes, bears some resemblance to that of the recent stop-motion stunner "Wildwood" — down to the flocks of malevolent ravens flapping about the place — can be only be coincidental, but "Hexed" isn't especially flattered by the comparison. It is, however, an emphatically more kid-friendly enterprise, and with "The Cat in the Hat" fizzling at the box office, the Disney pic should make hay with families over the Thanksgiving weekend. blogherads.adq.push(function () { blogherads .defineSlot( 'medrec', 'gpt-dsk-tab-mid-article2-uid1' ) .setTargeting( 'pos', ["mid","mid-article2","mid-articleX"] ) .setTargeting( 'viewable', 'yes' ) .setSubAdUnitPath("ros\/mid-article2") .addSize([[320,480],[300,250],[300,251],[2,4],[4,2],[620,366],[300,450]]) .setClsOptimization("minsize") ; });

A tone of chatty irreverence is struck by the opening prologue, which lays out a fairytale backstory in jagged, collage-style animation: a witch-ruled queendom, a power struggle, the loss or misplacement of magical powers that our blasé narrator describes as "a real bummer." She doesn't sound that invested, so neither are we. But as we begin the story proper in modern-day Salem, our interest is sparked in adorable, saucer-eyed newborn Billie — seemingly a typical baby girl, doted on by her single mom Alice (Rashida Jones), until one night in her crib, she demonstrates literal, lightning-like magic in her fingertips. Sadly the intriguing prospect of a telekinetic infant is quashed when, following a near escape from an otherworldly portal accidentally opened up by the tot, Alice neutralizes Billie's powers with an unprepossessing bracelet, and leaves Salem for Blahville, Ohio.

Sixteen-odd years later, Billie (now peppily voiced by Hailee Steinfeld ) is a strong-willed high-schooler wholly unaware of her powers, and chafing against her mom's constant, chiding attempts to control her. When the latest of Billie's rogue escapades gets her expelled from school, Alice decides again to leave town — at which point Billie, who has somehow never removed her safety bracelet until now, finally does so, and is immediately whooshed away into the magical realm of Hexe, and is immediately shown the strength of her witchy capabilities.

Those include flying — rare even among her newfound kind, and an immediate threat to Queen Celeste ( Jodie Foster ), the silver-coiffed sorceress who rules over Hexe with chic cruelty. Soon exasperatedly following her through the portal is Alice, who it turns out knows Hexe — and Celeste — all too well: No surprise that Billie's powers are hereditary, and that it falls to mother and daughter to save the embattled queendom, with some crotchety assistance from Beef (Walton Goggins), a three-eyed, Southern-drawled feline familiar who looks a little like Disney's Cheshire Cat as misremembered by ChatGPT. Goggins' ripe vernacular delivery is the most pleasingly unexpected element here: Everything else runs pretty much entirely according to studio-blueprinted plan, down to the breakneck, back-and-forth chase of a finale in which the real duel for dominance plays out on the soundtrack: Demi Lovato's "Confident" battles composer Kris Bowers' busy orchestrations to a cacophonous draw.

“Have you ever been persecuted, drowned or burned at the stake?” Conditions for entry to the city of Hexe are pretty rigorous and surprisingly dark in this engaging Disney animation. After playing things safe with 2023’s almost immediately forgettable, formulaic Wish , the studio has somehow turned the tanker round with a surprisingly edgy Y.A. fantasy that sometimes seems in danger of going too far in the opposite direction. Mention of warlocks in the stylish prologue is a little misleading; Hexed is a film about witches all the way, a hectic but mostly very entertaining fantasy that seems curiously beholden to Wicked , in ways that threaten to seriously undermine everything that’s good about it. blogherads.adq.push(function () { blogherads .defineSlot( 'medrec', 'gpt-dsk-tab-mid-article1-uid0' ) .setTargeting( 'pos', ["mid-article1","mid","mid-articleX","mid-article","300x251"] ) .setTargeting( 'viewable', 'yes' ) .setSubAdUnitPath("ros\/mid-article") .addSize([[2,2],[300,250],[620,350],[300,251],[501,282],[3,3],[2,4],[4,2],[620,366]]) .exemptFromSleep() .setClsOptimization("minsize") ; }); Related Stories Casting Hailee Steinfeld Confirms She's In 'Avengers: Doomsday' News How Jodie Foster Took Her First Disney Voice Role In 'Hexed' And Lent Her Smile To Her Character - Contenders L.A.

Girl power is the central theme, introducing Billie Doe ( Hailee Steinfeld ) as an Ohio infant with special powers, whose mother Alice ( Rashida Jones ) watches over her with a cautious eye after almost losing her to a couple of crows that once appeared through a portal to another world. Fast-forward a few years, and Billie is now going through her difficult teenage years, borrowing her mother’s car without permission (or a licence) to set the school mascot — significantly, an owl — free into the wild. The headmaster is on the warpath, but, while hiding in the bathroom, Billie manifests a strange ability to move things with her mind. Billie’s supernatural talents are somehow connected to a bracelet she has been forced to wear since childhood, and after she takes it off for a second time, the portal returns and sucks her into a parallel dimension. After being inducted by a talking book and a pen (Stephen Fry and Tracey Ullman respectively), Billie becomes a citizen of Hexe, a sanctuary city for practitioners of the occult. Hexe, though, is not quite the land of the free that it first appears to be; under the reign of Queen Celeste ( Jodie Foster ), it is very much a two-tier society, divided into those who indulge its narcissistic ruler and those who don’t. blogherads.adq.push(function () { blogherads .defineSlot( 'medrec', 'gpt-dl-mid-article-inject2-uid1' ) .setTargeting( 'pos', ["mid-article2","mid-articleX","mid-article","mid","300x251"] ) .setTargeting( 'viewable', 'yes' ) .setSubAdUnitPath("ros\/mid-article2") .addSize([[300,250],[300,251],[620,350],[2,4],[4,2],[620,366]]) .exemptFromSleep() .setClsOptimization("minsize") ; });

For reasons that seem fairly obvious already, Alice follows her daughter to Hexe and tries to send her home in an enchanted cauldron while she distracts the local police chief. Instead, however, Billie follows the cryptic label on a magic potion that leads her to Beef Roger Crummchuk ( Walton Goggins ), a three-eyed cat and one-time familiar to Queen Celeste’s daughter. After an extended sequence in which Billie begs for his help — lots of scenes gone on far too long — Beef Roger decides to help Billie look for Alice, who is now locked up behind barred doors and windows in a tower at the royal palace.

Comparisons with Wicked were always going to be inevitable, but the extent to which Hexed leans into them goes way beyond homage, notably in Queen Celeste’s fleet of flying bird-women with creepy fluorescent eyes. Hexe itself even looks like Emerald City, and when Billie first embarks on her adventure, she tells Beef Roger that “We’re gonna yellow-brick-road it”, the only time The Wizard of Oz is consciously mentioned. And once again, the climax involves the unmasking of an impostor, as Queen Celeste manipulates the talents of others to perform a centuries-old moon spell and gain ultimate power.

There’s still a lot to like, however, especially in its use of witchcraft as a metaphor; much play is made of Billie’s teenage-emo awkwardness, with her purple hair, spindly legs and clunky goth boots (“You think there’s something wrong with me,” she wails to her long-suffering mother). Surprisingly, there is no father in the picture, and the story boils down to an interesting three-way dynamic between Alice, her daughter and the Queen, one that doesn’t quite take the direction you might be expecting. A great and very eclectic voice cast helps in this regard, with Goggins a surprisingly calming presence whenever things get hectic (and they do).

But while Foster’s frosty Queen Celeste offers a refreshing return to the unreconstructed Disney villainesses of old, the rest of Hexed can’t help but seem retrofitted to get us there. There are welcome shades of Zootopia in its world-building — notably a town of familiars, and a rowdy pirate bar — but the story takes some strange turns, especially when, as Queen Celeste’s plan is about to unfold, we go back, albeit briefly, to Ohio. Its message — the usual be-yourself, do-your-thing — is harmless enough, mind. It’s just disappointing that a film so high on intention, ignition and inwitchification should fall so short in the inspiration department. There’s still enough potential for a sequel, mind.

articles.title: 'Focker-in-Law' Filmmaker John Hamburg Talks Ariana Grande's Comedic Timing and the Actor Who Made Ben Stiller Laugh Hardest on Set
articles.summary: Hamburg, whose credits include 'Me Time,' 'Why Him?,' 'I Love You, Man' and 'Along Came Polly,' reveals his writing technique and shares what it was like to be challenged by Grande: "She can dial it up or down and give me so many different levels."
articles.content:
It's been 26 years since Universal Pictures introduced Greg Focker to his girlfriend Pam's parents, Jack and Dina Byrnes, and audiences responded in kind — to the tune of $330 million worldwide. A franchise was born that year, and it has since produced 2004's Meet the Fockers , 2010's Little Fockers and the latest, Focker-in-Law , due in theaters Wednesday ahead of the Thanksgiving holiday. John Hamburg, who has been with the franchise since the beginning as a writer (and later as a producer), jumped into the director's chair on Focker-in-Law to direct a cast that includes returnees Ben Stiller , Robert De Niro , Teri Polo, Blythe Danner and Owen Wilson with new additions Ariana Grande , Skyler Gisondo , Beanie Feldstein and Eduardo Franco. The Hollywood Reporter caught up recently with Hamburg on Zoom to talk about landing a global pop superstar for the cast, his writing process and who makes Stiller laugh the hardest on set. blogherads.adq.push(function () { blogherads .defineSlot( 'medrec', 'gpt-article-mid-article-uid0' ) .setTargeting( 'pos', ["mid-article1","mid-articleX","mid","mid-article"] ) .setTargeting( 'viewable', 'yes' ) .setSubAdUnitPath("ros\/mid-article") .addSize([[300,250],[2,2],[300,251],[620,350],[2,4],[4,2],[320,480],[620,366],[300,450],[4,4],[300,251]]) .setClsOptimization("minsize") ; }); Related Stories Music Ariana Grande, Peacock Team on 'Eternal Sunshine Tour' Doc, Concert Film Movies 'Focker In-Law' Review: Ariana Grande Outshines Robert De Niro and Ben Stiller in an Otherwise Dire Fourth Installment

In 2020, you spoke with one of my colleagues who asked about the possibility of another movie. At the time you said, "I'll refrain from answering, but I love everyone involved, we’re all still in touch, and that’s all I’m going to say." An obvious follow-up: What happened?

I’m still asking myself that question. The core group has been making these movies for 26 years, and we check in from time to time. We only wanted to revisit these characters we love so much if we had a story we needed to tell. It wasn’t worth doing for the sake of it. Then we had a nugget: Ben Stiller is roughly the same age Robert De Niro was when we made the first movie, which is insane, but it gave us a way in. The first movie had an organic setup many people can relate to [bringing a significant other home to meet your parents], and it lead perfectly into the second. You met one set of parents, now it was time to meet the second set of in-laws. I don't think we had that clean of an idea for the third movie, which is maybe it was not quite as strong as the first two. For this movie, we looked inward and came to the conclusion that we wanted to get back to the simplicity of the original Meet the Parents. We had themes and ideas that we liked but it wasn't until we created the Olivia Jones character that everything came together. blogherads.adq.push(function () { blogherads .defineSlot( 'medrec', 'gpt-dsk-tab-mid-article2-uid1' ) .setTargeting( 'pos', ["mid","mid-article2","mid-articleX"] ) .setTargeting( 'viewable', 'yes' ) .setSubAdUnitPath("ros\/mid-article2") .addSize([[300,250],[300,251],[620,350],[2,4],[4,2],[320,480],[620,366],[300,450],[4,4]]) .setClsOptimization("minsize") ; });

Were you coming up with ideas and then taking it to the team, or brainstorming during meetings?

We did a little development when I was only producing. Once I came on as a writer, I explored different directions and we met over Zoom with the team — Ben, De Niro, Jane Rosenthal, Jay Roach and John Lesher — to talk things through. Then I went off into to a dark room to figure it out. I had the idea that Greg Focker’s nemesis could be his son’s girlfriend: a powerful, complex, formidable woman who is the opposite of Greg in every way he was 30 years ago. That felt compelling. I pitched to Jay Roach early on and asked what he thought.

In our conversations, Jay suggested different jobs she could have. I think that’s how we landed on the idea of her being a hostage negotiator. That clicked for me because suddenly I saw the central conflict: She thinks Greg is holding his son emotionally hostage by being such an overly involved parent. I got excited and pitched the team again. They liked it. I wrote a treatment of about 20 pages, telling the story and coming up with the pieces. After that, I had to fill everything in: Where is De Niro in his life? Who is Samantha, Beanie Feldstein’s character? Who is Henry, his son? But it all started with that idea.

I’m curious about your “dark room” strategy and how it’s changed over the years. When you need to lock yourself away and be productive, what does that look like for you? blogherads.adq.push(function () { blogherads .defineSlot( 'medrec', 'gpt-thr-article-mid-articleX-uid2' ) .setTargeting( 'pos', ["btf","mid-articleX","mid"] ) .setTargeting( 'viewable', 'yes' ) .setSubAdUnitPath("ros\/mid-articleX") .addSize([[300,250],[300,251],[620,350],[320,480],[620,366],[300,450],[4,4]]) .setLazyLoadMultiplier(2) .setClsOptimization("minsize") ; });

I write in 25-minute increments. There’s a productivity technique called the Pomodoro Technique . You shut everything off for 25 minutes and focus completely, then take a five-minute break and do the next one. If I get six of those in a day, I can be pretty productive. When I was rewriting the script during pre-production, I did 13 or 14 Pomodoros a day. There’s also a lot of hand-wringing and walking around my neighborhood. There are tears and moments when I think, "I can’t figure this story out. I don’t know what to do." It was challenging. Once I got the Olivia Jones character, the rest flowed quite smoothly.

Did you write with anyone in mind? At what point did Ariana Grande come into the mix?

If people are attached, I write with them in mind. I knew I was writing for Ben Stiller, Robert De Niro, Owen Wilson, Blythe Danner, Teri Polo and the others. But when I’m writing a script or early drafts, I usually want to make the characters real to me first. It’s almost like a police sketch of different people. I knew the energy and vibe, but wasn’t sure who would play the roles. Once I finished and put on my director's hat, I started thinking about who it could be. We landed on Ariana and said, "That's it. She has to be the one." I just hoped she would say yes because she was the only person I could think of, for a variety of reasons.

There are many wonderful actresses, but Ariana is such a force. The fact that she hasn’t been in a million movies makes her almost mysterious, which appealed to me. I’d watch her on Saturday Night Live and marvel at her incredible comic timing and think, "She's hilarious. She gets it." I also liked that she could be surprising. She has a twinkle in her eye and isn’t physically imposing, but the idea of someone who looks like Ariana Grande completely destroying Ben Stiller felt like a conflict we could really exploit. blogherads.adq.push(function () { blogherads .defineSlot( 'medrec', 'gpt-thr-article-mid-articleX-uid3' ) .setTargeting( 'pos', ["btf","mid-articleX","mid"] ) .setTargeting( 'viewable', 'yes' ) .setSubAdUnitPath("ros\/mid-articleX") .addSize([[300,250],[300,251],[620,350],[320,480],[620,366],[300,450],[4,4]]) .setLazyLoadMultiplier(2) .setClsOptimization("minsize") ; });

She pulls it off amazingly well. What was it like to direct her?

She's unbelievably smart, had a great handle on the character and pushed me to do more and try different things. As a writer, that’s what you want: someone who will challenge you and push you in the best ways, always in service of the story and character. She certainly did that. It's hard to believe she’s been in so few movies because she’s so skilled and has such a big toolbox. She can dial it up or down and give me so many different levels. That's great as a director: In the editing room, you can craft the performance and dial it up or down.

She announced that she was stepping away from public life. How did you respond to that news?

I love Ariana and have so much affection for her as a human being. When I heard the news, I also heard she was going to support the movie. We talk, and I know she loves it. I want whatever's best for her. At the end of the day, this is a business about human beings, and I adore her. I got to see her in concert in London this summer. It was moving to watch how her audience responds to her. She’s so powerful and gives so much. I thought, "My God, I can’t imagine what it’s like to give so much of yourself night after night." The key thing is that she said yes to the movie, and I know she’ll support it in whatever way feels right to her.

I got the chance to interview Skyler Gisondo for his recent Bonobos campaign and he told me that while he was shooting your movie with Ben Stiller, he didn't realize until he was on set how much he had borrowed from Ben during their first collaboration on The Night at the Museum franchise. What was it like to direct Ben and Skyler together? blogherads.adq.push(function () { blogherads .defineSlot( 'medrec', 'gpt-thr-article-mid-articleX-uid4' ) .setTargeting( 'pos', ["btf","mid-articleX","mid"] ) .setTargeting( 'viewable', 'yes' ) .setSubAdUnitPath("ros\/mid-articleX") .addSize([[300,250],[300,251],[620,350],[320,480],[620,366],[300,450],[4,4]]) .setLazyLoadMultiplier(2) .setClsOptimization("minsize") ; });

It was amazing. Skyler is one of those actors I’ve wanted to work with. You see someone like him in his movies, whether it's Booksmart or Licorice Pizza , and think, "I've got to work with that guy." I really liked the idea of Skyler as Henry Focker. I didn’t think it was a problem that he’d played Ben’s son before becuase it had been so long. I thought they’d have a shorthand, and they fell into it so quickly and were perfect. They both work hard and want to try different things. They push themselves to find nuance in the characters. I definitely saw Ben’s influence on Skyler. I could tell Skyler wasn’t just on set; he’d been taking it all in like a sponge. When you have someone like Ben Stiller — unbelievably funny and smart, and one of the hardest workers — that’s a great person to learn from. A lot of the movie's heart comes from the father-son relationship. There’s a really sweet moment between them at the end, and their real-life affection and long connection helped.

You've worked with Ben Stiller for years. When you're on set, what's the rhythm like?

One of the great things about our long relationship is that it's a real collaboration — a back-and-forth, a push-pull. He can pitch me things, and I can pitch him things. It's always about the character, the story and making it better. One thing I learned from Ben very early on, probably when we were working on Zoolander a thousand years ago, is never to settle. Keep pushing and trying things because they can always evolve and get a little better. He still has that ethos today. blogherads.adq.push(function () { blogherads .defineSlot( 'medrec', 'gpt-thr-article-mid-articleX-uid5' ) .setTargeting( 'pos', ["btf","mid-articleX","mid"] ) .setTargeting( 'viewable', 'yes' ) .setSubAdUnitPath("ros\/mid-articleX") .addSize([[300,250],[300,251],[620,350],[320,480],[620,366],[300,450],[4,4]]) .setLazyLoadMultiplier(2) .setClsOptimization("minsize") ; });

Directing Bob was truly one of the great joys of this experience. I’d directed Ben before and collaborated with him on many projects. I’d known Bob for years, primarily as a writer on the Meet the Parents movies. I’d helped him on a couple of other movies, uncredited, and was a writer-producer on the third one. But to direct him was a joy. He's Robert De Niro; his talent and filmography are second to none. What inspired me was that, at 82, he still had so much passion and enthusiasm. He'd call me late at night to pitch ideas, or share ideas constantly by email or text: "What about this for this scene?" How incredible is that? He has great instincts for Jack Burns and for how to humanize him.

You've also worked closely with Owen Wilson, who makes a fun return in this movie. Can you talk a bit about writing those scenes and working Owen?

I love Owen so much. I had the best time directing him in Stick . There’s no one like him: He has such a unique rhythm in the way he speaks and moves through life. It's so much fun to write a character who can say the most absurd things with a smile and no self-awareness. I can't have every character lack self-awareness, but Owen can parachute into the movie for a stretch and play that kind of character. In this movie, I thought about where he’d be in life. He has twins and thinks he's parenting them one-on-one, with no help, while there’s an army of nannies and caretakers everywhere. In his mind, he doesn’t believe he has any help; he’s raising the kids by himself. It’s so much fun to write. blogherads.adq.push(function () { blogherads .defineSlot( 'medrec', 'gpt-thr-article-mid-articleX-uid6' ) .setTargeting( 'pos', ["btf","mid-articleX","mid"] ) .setTargeting( 'viewable', 'yes' ) .setSubAdUnitPath("ros\/mid-articleX") .addSize([[300,250],[300,251],[620,350],[320,480],[620,366],[300,450],[4,4]]) .setLazyLoadMultiplier(2) .setClsOptimization("minsize") ; });

One of the other great joys is that no one makes Ben laugh like Owen Wilson. They’re so different, so close, and have made so many great movies together, but they live life as total opposites. Owen cracks Ben up; he just has his number. It’s so much fun to watch them enjoy each other’s company between takes. When the camera’s rolling, there’s a tension that’s fun to film and explore.

What was the most challenging nut to crack?

It started with figuring out who Greg Focker’s adversary would be, which I've touched on. But the most challenging scene was probably the bike race. In my early drafts, it was on a tennis court, and that didn’t work for a variety of reasons. I also knew Ben was into the Tour de France and cycled himself, so I thought he might like it. A director friend who read it said, "Why'd you do a bike scene? They’re so hard to shoot." It was a nightmare, but we had the right team in place, and it went smoothly. Set pieces can’t be there just for their own sake; they have to be about character and the tension between the characters. I had to figure out the setting and the sport. The Meet the Parents movies have a tradition of a sport going wrong — pool volleyball in the first movie, football in the second — so I knew I’d have a sports scene. I just didn’t land on it until later in the process.

In an interview, Barbra Streisand revealed that she was still upset over her salary for the Fockers . Were you close to getting her for this movie, or were there conversations? blogherads.adq.push(function () { blogherads .defineSlot( 'medrec', 'gpt-thr-article-mid-articleX-uid7' ) .setTargeting( 'pos', ["btf","mid-articleX","mid"] ) .setTargeting( 'viewable', 'yes' ) .setSubAdUnitPath("ros\/mid-articleX") .addSize([[300,250],[300,251],[620,350],[320,480],[620,366],[300,450],[4,4]]) .setLazyLoadMultiplier(2) .setClsOptimization("minsize") ; });

Barbra and Dustin are such a part of the Fockerverse , and I’m grateful every day that they were in those two movies. With this movie, I really wanted to return to the simplicity of the original Meet the Parents. Sequels can get bigger, with more and more characters, so I set this movie in the Burns family home, where the original took place, and tried to keep it contained. I love Dustin and Barbra. We did talk about it, of course, because they’re part of our Focker family. But with so many new characters in this generation, it ultimately felt right to focus on the characters we ended up with.

People keep talking about the challenging landscape for feature film comedies in theaters. How hard is it to be a comedy writer and filmmaker in the business right now? Do you feel the pressure?

When these movies are made well, there’s nothing better than sitting with 400 people who are all laughing and cringing. That’s why I got into this business: I loved going to the movies and laughing my butt off. I mourned the fact that comedies disappeared from studio film slates and theaters. They moved to streaming, which is great, but it’s not quite the same for a movie like this. That also sets up all the different ways people will see the movie later. I’m hopeful. I just wrote and directed a movie that’s being released in theaters, so of course I have some skin in the game. But I do think people are realizing that we need to be together. Watching things alone at home or on our phones is great for some things, but it isn’t everything. I’m optimistic this genre can come back. blogherads.adq.push(function () { blogherads .defineSlot( 'medrec', 'gpt-thr-article-mid-articleX-uid8' ) .setTargeting( 'pos', ["btf","mid-articleX","mid"] ) .setTargeting( 'viewable', 'yes' ) .setSubAdUnitPath("ros\/mid-articleX") .addSize([[300,250],[300,251],[620,350],[320,480],[620,366],[300,450],[4,4]]) .setLazyLoadMultiplier(2) .setClsOptimization("minsize") ; });

As for pressure, my comedy-director friends are constantly asking, "How did the movie test? Is it good? Is this movie going to work?" I tell them it tested great. I don’t know how it will do, but I feel good about it. I do feel some pressure because I love this genre. It’s given me everything in my career, and I’m hopeful we can get back to a place where these movies are seen in theaters again.

When was the last time you saw something and reached out to say, "God, that was funny,” or “I loved that”?

Literally the other day. I saw an ad Ben Stiller did for his soda brand, Stiller Soda. He goes to Canter’s Deli, gets it wrong, and is dressed like he’s in the cast of Andrew Lloyd Webber’s Cats . It was hysterical. I texted him a crying-laughing emoji. It was pretty damn funny. And my God, the Nathan Fielder and Lance Oppenheim movie — the first half had me thinking, "Wow, there are big laughs in this. Huge laughs." It’s so awkward, but it was really funny. articles.title: ‘Hexed’ Review: Hailee Steinfeld and Rashida Jones Lead a Disney Fantasy More Enchanting in Its Spectacle Than Its Storytelling
articles.summary: Jodie Foster and Walton Goggins also lend their voices to the animated adventure about a teenager who discovers she's a witch and gets transported to a magical realm.
articles.content:
There’s a sequence midway through Hexed , Disney’s animated fantasy adventure, when mother-daughter heroines Alice ( Rashida Jones ) and Billie ( Hailee Steinfeld ) are forced to retreat to a remote lakeside cabin. Coming just after a brutal face-off with the wicked queen Celeste ( Jodie Foster ), the scene is heavy with emotion; whether they’re able to pull off a miraculous recovery here will determine the fate of not only their mission, but their very lives.

Amid all that fear and hope and desperate love, however, I found myself overcome by an incongruous surge of envy. As I looked around the hideaway, with its giant windows and twinkly fairy lights, its big fluffy couch perfect for napping and its rustic shelves crammed with plants and candles and otherworldly knickknacks, I couldn't help thinking: I would kill to rent this place on Airbnb . blogherads.adq.push(function () { blogherads .defineSlot( 'medrec', 'gpt-article-mid-article-uid0' ) .setTargeting( 'pos', ["mid-article1","mid-articleX","mid","mid-article"] ) .setTargeting( 'viewable', 'yes' ) .setSubAdUnitPath("ros\/mid-article") .addSize([[300,250],[2,2],[300,251],[620,350],[2,4],[4,2],[320,480],[620,366],[300,450],[4,4],[300,251]]) .setClsOptimization("minsize") ; }); Related Stories Movies Hailee Steinfeld on Recording Music for New Movie 'Hexed' and Becoming a Mother in the Process Movies Jodie Foster Describes 'F1' as a Movie "Made by AI" at Aspen Ideas Fest: "I Don't Say This Disparagingly" Hexed The Bottom Line You've heard this story, but you haven't seen this world. Release date: Wednesday, Nov. 25 Cast: Hailee Steinfeld, Rashida Jones, Walton Goggins, Jodie Foster, Dan Stevens, Henry Winkler Directors: Fawn Veerasunthorn, Jason Hand Screenwriters: Jared Bush, Dana Ledoux Miller Rated PG, 1 hour 43 minutes

It wasn’t the first time watching the film that I’d wished I could walk right into the screen, though it was surely the only time I could imagine the rental listing so clearly. More than as a fairy tale, an inspirational fable or a complex exploration of the bonds between mothers and daughters, Hexed shines brightest as a travelogue through an enchanting world only accessible through the portal of a screen. If that’s not enough to make for a new cinematic classic, it’s more than enough to make for a pleasurably transportive trip to the theater.

The actual premise, as scripted by Jared Bush and Dana Ledoux Miller (the recent live-action Moana ) and directed by Fawn Veerasunthorn ( Wish ) and Jason Hand ( Moana 2 ), is a hodgepodge of sturdy but shopworn clichés. Like teens everywhere since time immemorial, Billie (Steinfeld) has never quite felt like she fits in. Unlike most teens, Billie turns out to have a very good reason for feeling this way. A dust-up at her suburban Ohio high school reveals Billie to be not an ordinary girl but a witch, her powers suppressed at infancy by her overprotective mother, Alice. blogherads.adq.push(function () { blogherads .defineSlot( 'medrec', 'gpt-dsk-tab-mid-article2-uid1' ) .setTargeting( 'pos', ["mid","mid-article2","mid-articleX"] ) .setTargeting( 'viewable', 'yes' ) .setSubAdUnitPath("ros\/mid-article2") .addSize([[300,250],[300,251],[620,350],[2,4],[4,2],[320,480],[620,366],[300,450],[4,4]]) .setClsOptimization("minsize") ; });

In short order, Billie finds herself transported to Hexe, a magical realm awaiting the fulfillment of a prophecy by a chosen one who will finally bring true freedom and safety to all of its people. Blah blah blah, and so on and so forth; Hexed doesn’t seem especially interested in the specifics of this situation, so you needn’t concern yourself with them either. The more important thing is that this plot functions very capably as an excuse to zip around the land of Hexe, which is where the real fun lies.

As experienced through Billie and then Alice — you didn’t expect this helicopter mom not to have a Find My Kid app installed, did you? — Hexe is a riotous feast of deep colors, rich textures and undulating shapes. It is both the film’s blessing and its curse that a standard phone or laptop, of the sort you may have used to view the trailer, cannot do it justice. What looks merely messy on an eight-inch screen looks wonderfully immersive on a 20-foot one, the frame crowded with so much fine detail it seems impossible to take it all in at once.

Courtesy of production designer Lorelay Bové, the characters dance through Disney-land cute towns, trudge through Avatar -alien swamps, curl up in goblincore dens packed with funny little cat tchotchkes. In my very favorite sequence, they don animal disguises to infiltrate a no-humans-allowed dive where a cockroach and a spider are engaging in a WWE-style match, down to a teeny-tiny folding chair. It was such a rowdy good time, I was sorry when our heroes finally retrieved what they had come for and were thus able to leave. blogherads.adq.push(function () { blogherads .defineSlot( 'medrec', 'gpt-thr-article-mid-articleX-uid2' ) .setTargeting( 'pos', ["btf","mid-articleX","mid"] ) .setTargeting( 'viewable', 'yes' ) .setSubAdUnitPath("ros\/mid-articleX") .addSize([[300,250],[300,251],[620,350],[320,480],[620,366],[300,450],[4,4]]) .setLazyLoadMultiplier(2) .setClsOptimization("minsize") ; });

The imaginative world-building extends to an amusingly idiosyncratic supporting cast. Walton Goggins steals every one of his scenes as Beef Roger Crummchuk, a green three-eyed cat who’d rather be drinking martinis alone in his magically expanded swamp RV. Lazy and cantankerous in equal measure, he’s both the film’s most reliable comic highlight and its unexpected heart — the cynic who goes from insisting that “it’s safer to stay home licking your armpit” since “most battles aren't worth fighting” anyway to finding a renewed sense of hope in Billie’s determined heroism.

Really, the whole ensemble is an embarrassment of riches, with even one-scene characters played by the very recognizable likes of Jimmy O. Yang or Ron Funches or Stephen Fry. It’s surely an expensive flex from Disney, but it’s one that pays off. Hexe feels as vivid as it does because Hexed misses no opportunity to stuff in a bit more humor or personality or strangeness around the margins. A tense conversation with the queen might be punctuated by a tiny teacup exclaiming, “Baby, you’re cooked ” in the voice of Yvette Nicole Brown, or an impromptu spell-casting practice session interrupted by the complaints of a microwave voiced by Wayne Knight.

In comparison to all the bewitching delights and exotic thrills of Hexe, Billie and Alice almost cannot help but pale in comparison. The big lessons Alice and Billie come away with (Mom realizes she can’t shelter her little girl forever, said girl learns to see Mom as her own person) are as predictable as they are unimpeachably timeless. articles.title: Four-Day Rom-Com Film Festival to Launch in Santa Barbara
articles.summary: The inaugural event is set for April 22–25, 2027.
articles.content:
Romantic comedies are feeling the love.

The genre is getting its own cinematic celebration with the inaugural Rom-Com Film Festival, launching in Santa Barbara April 22- 25, 2027. The event will bring together filmmakers and audiences for four days of toasting the classics and discovering new stories, after being founded by Carissa Buffel, Kevin Matusow and Kate Bacon of women-owned production company The Traveling Picture Show Company.

“ Rom-coms make people smile. It’s really as simple as that. We wanted to create a festival that celebrates this beloved genre and brings people together in a lighthearted and happy way," Bacon said in a statement. Screenings will take place across multiple venues in downtown Santa Barbara, including the McHurley Film Center and the Santa Barbara Museum of Art, with an additional outdoor screening experience in the works. Film submissions are now open for the inaugural Rom-Com Film Festival, inviting filmmakers to share their work for consideration in the festival's 2027 program. Share on X (Opens in new window) X Share on Facebook (Opens in new window) Facebook Add Us On Google A new dark fantasy Isekai anime is coming to Crunchyroll this January, and has now locked down its release date with a new trailer and poster showing it all off. With the ongoing slate of Fall 2026 anime releases now rounding out their respective final phases, it's time to look ahead to all of the new releases coming our way next year. And 2027 looks like it's going to be kicking things off on the right foot for Isekai anime fans with one series in particular.

The anime adaptation for Yu Shimizu and Makoto Aogiri's Otherworldly Munchkin: Let's Speedrun the Dungeon with Only 1 HP! was originally scheduled for a release in Fall 2025 before being hit by a major production delay behind the scenes. But it's finally now set a release date of January 7th next year as part of the upcoming Winter 2027 slate. To commemorate the release of the new series, you can check out the new trailer and poster for the upcoming Isekai below.

Otherworldly Munchkin: Let's Speedrun the Dungeon with Only 1 HP! is currently scheduled to release in Japan on January 7th, and will be streaming exclusively with Crunchyroll when it finally makes its debut. There have been quite a few shake ups behind the scenes following its two year delay too with Naoya Fukushi now directing the series for Studio Durandal with Mamoru Yokota and Yui Kato providing the character designs, Yui Horiguchi serving as CG director, Hiroshi Hosokawa providing the scripts, and Asami Tachibana composing the music.

It's also been confirmed that Otherworldly Munchkin: Let's Speedrun the Dungeon with Only 1 HP! will feature the opening theme titled "Sai" as performed by LIL LEAGUE, and an ending theme titled "Zanka" as performed by ZAQ. Both of which have been previewed in this newly released trailer. The voice cast for the series includes Kazuki Ura as Yukito Kirihara, Kana Yuki as Charlotte R. Brownia, Yui Ishikawa as Lumilia Sherwood, Kaori Maeda as Liverna Dark, Hika Tsukishiro as Sana Kirihara, Fukushi Ochiai as Rocinante, Ayasa Ito as Managarmr, Yoko Hikasa as Nephilia Curse, Anri Katsu as the narrator, and Yuichiro Umehara as Sharaza.

Otherworldly Munchkin: Let's Speedrun the Dungeon with Only 1 HP! takes a dark path much like some of the Isekai anime releases that have gotten a lot of attention from fans in the last few years. Yukito and his sister are suddenly transported to another world, but he's got a major disadvantage in exploring it. When he's brought to this new world he's given a mysterious character sheet and given all sorts of random properties by a mysterious woman.

Discovering he only has a single hit point, Yukito needs to navigate this mysterious new world and find his sister all while dealing with some strange new threats. There's some of kind of underlying threat underneath it all, and that always leads to some great results with Isekai anime of this kind. With so many other new Isekai coming our way next year , what are you hoping to see in action in 2027? Let us know all of your thoughts about it in the comments.

articles.title: Chris Evans Just Confirmed a Big Avengers: Doomsday Theory, And Marvel Fans Shouldn't Be Surprised
articles.summary: Marvel Studios Robert Downey Jr. is wearing that Doom mask for all of Avengers: Doomsday, and that's according to MCU favorite Chris Evans. Since Marvel Studios confirmed that the Oscar-winning Downey would return to the fold but take on the part of Doctor Doom rather than Tony Stark, fans have speculated about the real reason behind it. […]
articles.content:
Share on X (Opens in new window) X Share on Facebook (Opens in new window) Facebook Add Us On Google Robert Downey Jr. is wearing that Doom mask for all of Avengers: Doomsday , and that's according to MCU favorite Chris Evans . Since Marvel Studios confirmed that the Oscar-winning Downey would return to the fold but take on the part of Doctor Doom rather than Tony Stark, fans have speculated about the real reason behind it . Could Doom be some kind of variant of Iron Man, or vice versa? In any event, every Marvel fan is already bracing for the moment that Doom's mask comes off on screen and the MCU heroes see that familiar face, if they do at all.

Speaking with Empire , though, Chris Evans says that Robert Downey Jr. keeps the mask on for the entire movie. “He's wearing a mask the whole time," Evans said. "That's not an easy challenge, to try and get your message across and be emotionally available to connect with. It just reinforces what I've always felt: Downey can do anything.” The Captain America star's confirmation about Doomsday seems to squash any fan theory about Downey's face being seen in the film as a big reveal…or does it?

It's worth reiterating that Evans said his co-star is "wearing a mask the entire time," and not "you never see Robert Downey Jr.'s face." Evans could be truthful here about how often Doom is wearing his signature mask; it would be in keeping with decades of comic book canon (though Anthony Mackie already spilled the beans that "it wasn't" him on set sometimes ), but that doesn't mean that there won't be a moment where Doom is isolated and takes it off for a moment.

That said, it's also easy to see why a performer like Robert Downey Jr. would be able to reach the emotional depths required of Victor Von Doom and the tragic backstory that has pushed him to his limits , despite wearing a mask; it's all about how he uses his eyes across the film. Though we've only seen so much footage of Doom in the trailers for the film, the close-ups of his eyes reveal that there's a nuanced performance happening under there.

If it ends up being true that Robert Downey Jr. is wearing his Doom mask for the entire film, it could be because Marvel is saving the big unmasking moment for Avengers: Secret Wars . Fans are already bracing for RDJ's villain to win at the end of the day and set up the next big crossover movie, which could very well be where Tony Stark's former allies see the villain who destroyed the multiverse bear a striking resemblance to the hero that saved their own world. It will be a devastating reveal at any point, but it simply remains to be seen when Marvel decides to deploy it.

What do you think? Is Evans telling the truth, and does Robert Downey Jr. wears the Doom mask the entire movie? Or is he simply preserving the Marvel spoiler secrets and we'll see him without the mask at some point? Sound off with your thoughts in the comments below and let us know.

articles.title: Josh Allen on 'The Buffalo Miracle,' and What a Miracle It Would Be to Bring Buffalo a Super Bowl
articles.summary: The superstar quarterback's production company Out of Pocket is off to a hot start — much like the 9-1 Bills.
articles.content:
Buffalo is the coldest place with the warmest neighbors.

That dichotomy of sorts is on full display in HBO 's The Buffalo Miracle , an Oscar-qualifying documentary short executive produced by Buffalo Bills quarterback Josh Allen , among others. The Buffalo Miracle tells the story of the Buffalo, New York residents who came together during the deadly Christmas blizzard of 2022. Their refuge? McDonald's store #34815.

Though Allen is the big name here, The Buffalo Miracle centers on a different, shorter local hero: McDonald's manager Kristin Kosha bucked corporate protocol, unlocking the fast-food restaurant's doors to more than 50 stranded, freezing residents as the historic storm grew increasingly dangerous. (Also north of 50? The inches of snow dumped by the Dec. 23-27 blizzard.) Lives were saved and bonds were formed. And oh yeah, there was a Bills game to watch and pass the time — they crushed the Chicago Bears in Chicago, 35-13, clinching the AFC East. blogherads.adq.push(function () { blogherads .defineSlot( 'medrec', 'gpt-article-mid-article-uid0' ) .setTargeting( 'pos', ["mid-article1","mid-articleX","mid","mid-article"] ) .setTargeting( 'viewable', 'yes' ) .setSubAdUnitPath("ros\/mid-article") .addSize([[300,250],[2,2],[300,251],[620,350],[2,4],[4,2],[320,480],[620,366],[300,450],[4,4],[300,251]]) .setClsOptimization("minsize") ; }); Related Stories TV Archie Renaux on 'War's Resident -- and Misunderstood -- Bad Boy TV 'The Gilded Age' Scores Season 5 Renewal at HBO

Kosha, since promoted to area supervisor, tells The Hollywood Reporter her "regular customers" are "counting down the days" to the HBO and HBO Max premiere — a number that just today hit zero. Also, she got a real kick out of seeing herself animated (pictured below).

"I love it! It’s not every day you get to see yourself drawn as a cartoon," Kosha said. "Honestly, it made me laugh, but it also made me feel a little emotional. It’s a fun reminder that what our team did during that storm meant something to people, and I’m proud to represent my crew and this community in any form, animated or not." blogherads.adq.push(function () { blogherads .defineSlot( 'medrec', 'gpt-dsk-tab-mid-article2-uid1' ) .setTargeting( 'pos', ["mid","mid-article2","mid-articleX"] ) .setTargeting( 'viewable', 'yes' ) .setSubAdUnitPath("ros\/mid-article2") .addSize([[300,250],[300,251],[620,350],[2,4],[4,2],[320,480],[620,366],[300,450],[4,4]]) .setClsOptimization("minsize") ; });

The Buffalo Miracle , directed by two-time Academy Award winner Ben Proudfoot ( The Last Repair Shop and The Queen of Basketball ), is half original animation (hand-drawn 2D, miniatures and stop motion) and half live-action. It premiered earlier this year at Telluride.

Days after his Nov. 15, 2026 dismantling of the New York Jets , THR caught up with Allen via Zoom. The conversation ranged from his plans for new production company Out of Pocket to the recent YouTube Golf Internet Invitational to, of course, his McDonald's order. Read our Q&A, below.

Out of Pocket was announced just before the NFL Regular Season. You're CEO, you're going to executive produce all of the output: How much time, if any, will you be able to dedicate to Out of Pocket during the football season?

I mean, it's not going to be every single week. But given certain… whether we have a Thursday night game, if we can get on a phone call and talk with my team, who's been doing a fantastic job, and just run down what's going on. Watching shorts and seeing if we want to attach our name with them.

But this one kind of coincidentally came up right when we launched. We got introduced to Ben [Proudfoot] from a mutual friend, and it just worked out perfectly. I loved the story and figured, if we can get my name and my team and NFL Films behind it, what it could be. Ben did such a great job. We trusted his vision, and obviously he's a two-time Academy winner, so he knows exactly what he's doing. But very, very fortunate to be working on this with him. blogherads.adq.push(function () { blogherads .defineSlot( 'medrec', 'gpt-thr-article-mid-articleX-uid2' ) .setTargeting( 'pos', ["btf","mid-articleX","mid"] ) .setTargeting( 'viewable', 'yes' ) .setSubAdUnitPath("ros\/mid-articleX") .addSize([[300,250],[300,251],[620,350],[320,480],[620,366],[300,450],[4,4]]) .setLazyLoadMultiplier(2) .setClsOptimization("minsize") ; });

What are your immediate plans for Out of Pocket once your season ends?

We've got some cool projects coming up. We've got a scripted show that I can't talk a lot about, but just got sold, and we're working on that right now. That's going to be awesome. We've got some digital media — a little golf channel coming out with me and three buddies — a couple more projects that are in the works right now. Honestly, it's happened extremely quickly.

My team is doing such a great job of keeping things on track, especially during the season when I can't be there. But it's been a whirlwind. I've learned a lot over the last six months, but I'm very grateful to be doing it. It's something I never really thought I would be getting into. But given my love of sports, I think there is still a lot of stories out there that can be told — whether it's through scripted, non-scripted, digital, whatever it is — and I think that's something that we're we're trying to capitalize on.

The digital golf channel you're referring to — I assume you mean YouTube Golf?

Did you get to watch any of the Internet Invitational? I just interviewed Robby Berger ( Bob Does Sports ) for the finale .

I've spoken with LeBron James about this too: It's so funny how the absolute top athletes in the world with the widest primetime-television reach geek out over amateur golf people watch on their phones.

It's fun. In a sense, you get to take the mask off, right? You get to show who you are off the field, who you are in a more fun environment when you're with a couple buddies. Kevin Hart launched his and I know Bobby Berger very well. We've golfed against them a couple times, so I've been on his channels. It's just a way for us to get out there, express who we really yeah in a nice light, and have fun and playing golf while doing it — it doesn't suck. blogherads.adq.push(function () { blogherads .defineSlot( 'medrec', 'gpt-thr-article-mid-articleX-uid3' ) .setTargeting( 'pos', ["btf","mid-articleX","mid"] ) .setTargeting( 'viewable', 'yes' ) .setSubAdUnitPath("ros\/mid-articleX") .addSize([[300,250],[300,251],[620,350],[320,480],[620,366],[300,450],[4,4]]) .setLazyLoadMultiplier(2) .setClsOptimization("minsize") ; });

Your wife is the very successful actress Hailee Steinfeld — has she been advising on Out of Pocket?

Yes, she is special advisory for sure. She's helped out with a lot of things in terms of just, like, mentally processing some of the stuff. And in the future, we plan on doing some some fun stuff together. It's awesome to have her as someone I can lean on and ask questions and to have answers immediately, so it's works out really well.

Do you have any ambition to act?

I don't think so. I think staying behind the camera is the best option for me. I'll let my wife get in front.

You're extremely creative on the football field. Do you believe the creative football mind informs the creative artistic mind and vice-versa?

Yeah, I pride myself on the creativity that I have on the football field, and I think in order— the football field, in my opinion, is the truest version of who you are as a person, right? That is everything stripped off. That is you going out there and you are letting your emotions show. You are as vulnerable as anybody in the world when those cameras are on you and you're trying to compete to win, so I definitely think that's who I am, and it's really no different off the field. I try to have the most fun that I can. I know it's a very serious job, but I find the light in almost anything and everything — sometimes to a fault But that's exactly who I am, and [Out of Pocket] is an outlet for me to express that in a different way.

Have you been to the specific McDonald's in the doc? blogherads.adq.push(function () { blogherads .defineSlot( 'medrec', 'gpt-thr-article-mid-articleX-uid4' ) .setTargeting( 'pos', ["btf","mid-articleX","mid"] ) .setTargeting( 'viewable', 'yes' ) .setSubAdUnitPath("ros\/mid-articleX") .addSize([[300,250],[300,251],[620,350],[320,480],[620,366],[300,450],[4,4]]) .setLazyLoadMultiplier(2) .setClsOptimization("minsize") ; });

They're like 35 minutes north. I have not been to that McDonald's, but I get to meet Kristin and (assistant manager) Jeff Spengler tonight, so that'll be really fun.

I'm not gonna lie, I'm a Big Mac guy, and give me 10 nuggets and a large fry. And you've gotta have the Oreo McFlurry.

The Bills have never won a Super Bowl. When they famously lost four straight in the '90s, you hadn't yet been born. Do you think you're able to understand how much a Super Bowl win would mean to Buffalo?

I think so. I've come to grips with [the fact that] I think it's going to mean more to the city than it will to me personally. The amount of people who are going to express a lot of emotion when that happens is going to be awesome to see. I picture that parade. I have dreams about it. articles.title: Fans Were Mad After A Wedding Guest Ignored Miley Cyrus’ Dress Code. Now, Her Sister Spoke Out

The guest who wore yellow is Belgica Vargas, the wife of the music producer Shawn Everett, and in photos from the ceremony, she can be seen in a yellow outfit among a sea of people wearing black. The photo caused many people on Reddit to comment things like:

Meanwhile, many others on Reddit gave her the benefit of the doubt, saying she probably missed the memo on the dress code. Those more sympathetic Reddit commenters wrote things like:

Then, there was a whole camp of folks who were upset about there being a dress code in the first place. So, all around, this yellow outfit is causing quite the stir online. However, Vargas’ sister has popped into the comments to clarify how this seemingly happened.

It turns out that comment about the woman in yellow just never getting the memo about the dress code was a great guess. As this fashion slip up went viral, Vargas sister, Grecia commented on a video of someone zooming in on her sibling’s dress. Explaining that her sister was not aware of the dress code, she wrote:

Listen, it’s easy to miss details sometimes. And I know I’ve missed details and dress codes before. Things happen, and in this case, the message about the all-black dress code seemingly wasn’t passed along.

articles.title: Tidal Bans Wholly AI-Generated Music: "Serious Problem That Has Only Increased in Scale"
articles.summary: The service said Tuesday that more than 60 percent of new tracks uploaded to its service on Nov. 6 were fully AI-generated songs.
articles.content:
Tidal is outlawing wholly AI-generated music from its platform, the streaming service announced on Tuesday, saying that AI music "diverts streams and royalties away from the artists, and confuses fans."

"To ensure Tidal remains the best place for artists to share their work, and for listeners to enjoy it, we’re removing all tracks that we determine are 100% AI generated," Tidal said in a social media post on Tuesday. "We’re also banning distributors from delivering these tracks to us, and will reject deliveries if their metadata says they were generated solely using AI tools."

Tracks that were made with assistance from AI will still be allowed. The new ban will go into effect December 9.

Tidal said it's seen an influx of AI-generated tracks on its platform over the past several months, noting that in the past 90 days, about 43 percent of tracks distributed on the platform were identified as wholly AI-generated. On Nov. 6 alone, 60 percent of newly uploaded songs were AI tracks. But despite the growing number of songs, 96 percent of those tracks have generated zero streams.

"Wholly AI-generated music intended to mislead listeners and impersonate artists is another serious problem that has only increased in scale," Tidal said. "It’s true that not all songs catch on immediately, and artists should have time to build their fanbases. But this situation is different – at this scale, the authentic music and artists that Tidal subscribers are looking to listen to and discover get buried."

With its decision Tuesday, Tidal now has the most stringent anti-AI policies among the music streaming services, and one of the few notable platforms beyond Bandcamp, the music distribution service popular among indie artists, to have outright banned AI music. While Spotify and Apple Music, the two largest DSPs, have taken steps to either label AI tracks and artists or remove them from recommendations, they still allow fully-generated songs to get uploaded to their respective platforms.

Fans and the music industry alike have voiced their frustration about AI music flooding streaming platforms. On an earnings call in October , Universal Music Group CEO Lucian Grainge advocated for streaming services to pay out AI-generated tracks less than music from human artists, arguing that AI slop degrades the fan experience and diverts value from real artists," and that removing the profit motive would disincentivize “industrial scale content production.”

He also produced the first four films in The Hunger Games franchise.

“It’s an honor to be part of Jana’s beautiful film that skillfully blends a lifetime of Bob’s personal archives with a front row look behind the scenes of some of the greatest films and greatest directors of the last 40 years. As Quentin T says in the film, ‘There is Robert Richardson and there is everyone else,’” said Kilik.

Robert Richardson: The White Devil traces the unlikely creative partnership between Hojdová and the cinematographer, when she was a cinematography student at Prague’s FAMU film academy, and reached out to him for a university project.

Featuring Richardson alongside filmmakers Stone, Scorsese and Tarantino, as well as Kate Hudson and Woody Harrelson, the documentary explores Richardson’s creative vision, uncompromising artistic temperament and extraordinary career.

I had the privilege of interviewing the cast ahead of the movie's release, where I asked Hawke if any scenes of her character ended up on the cutting room floor. She told me:

Despite being a franchise about young people killing each other, The Hunger Games movies have all been PG-13. As such, Lawrence and company have to be specific about how violent the imagery can be. While I wanted to see more of Wiress, Hawke maintains that it would have been too "disturbing" to watch the beloved Victor being tortured by President Snow's forces. She's probably not wrong, as much as I wanted to see more of her take on the character.

Later in our same conversation, Maya Hawke explained the upside of not having to shoot these difficult scenes as Wiress. As she told me:

Obviously Hawke would have crushed it if we saw Wiress' torture and interrogation, but that ultimately wasn't something that was ever going to be part of Sunrise on the Reaping. In our chat I asked the Do Revenge actress if Wiress had a mental break as a result of her torture, transforming her into the character we were introduced to by Amanda Plummer in Catching Fire . She confirmed to me:

I've still got FOMO about not getting more of Wiress, but I understand why it didn't happen. After all, Sunrise on the Reaping is a story about Haymitch above all.
